{{short description|Chinese mathematician and computer scientist}}
'''Hao Huang''' ({{Lang-zh|c=黄皓|p=Huáng Hào}}) is a Chinese mathematician known for solving the [[sensitivity conjecture]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://phys.org/news/2019-07-mathematician-proof-sensitivity-conjecture.html|title=Mathematician to present a proof of the Sensitivity Conjecture|website=phys.org|language=en-us|access-date=2019-12-21}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/mathematician-solves-computer-science-conjecture-in-two-pages-20190725/|title=Decades-Old Computer Science Conjecture Solved in Two Pages|last=Klarreich|first=Erica|website=Quanta Magazine|date=25 July 2019 |language=en|access-date=2019-12-21}}</ref> Huang is currently an associate professor in the mathematics department at [[National University of Singapore]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://blog.nus.edu.sg/huanghao/|title=Welcome to Hao Huang's homepage|access-date=2021-08-14}}</ref>

Huang received a [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] degree in [[mathematics]] at [[Peking University]] in 2007.<ref name=":0" /> He obtained his Ph.D. in mathematics from his dissertation titled ''Various Problems in Extremal Combinatorics'' from the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA) in 2012 advised by [[Benny Sudakov]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=166481|title=Hao Huang - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu|access-date=2019-12-21}}</ref> His postdoctoral research was done at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey]] and [[DIMACS]] at [[Rutgers University]] in 2012–2014, followed by a year at the [[Institute for Mathematics and its Applications]] at the [[University of Minnesota]]. Huang then became an assistant professor from 2015 to 2021 in the Department of Mathematics at [[Emory University]].<ref name=":0" />

In July 2019, Huang announced a breakthrough, which gave a proof of the sensitivity conjecture.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Huang|first=Hao|date=2019|title=Induced subgraphs of hypercubes and a proof of the Sensitivity Conjecture|journal=Annals of Mathematics|volume=190|issue=3|pages=949–955|doi=10.4007/annals.2019.190.3.6|issn=0003-486X|jstor=10.4007/annals.2019.190.3.6|bibcode=2019arXiv190700847H|arxiv=1907.00847|s2cid=195767594}}</ref> At that point the conjecture had been open for nearly 30 years, having been posed by [[Noam Nisan]] and [[Mario Szegedy]] in 1992.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Nisan|first1=Noam|last2=Szegedy|first2=Mario|title=Proceedings of the twenty-fourth annual ACM symposium on Theory of computing - STOC '92 |chapter=On the degree of Boolean functions as real polynomials |date=1992|location=New York, NY, USA|publisher=ACM|pages=462–467|doi=10.1145/129712.129757|isbn=978-0-89791-511-3|s2cid=6919144|doi-access=free}}</ref> Huang has received positive attention for his discovery, as theoretical computer scientist [[Scott Aaronson]] described, "I find it hard to imagine that even God knows how to prove the Sensitivity Conjecture in any simpler way than this."<ref>[https://www.quantamagazine.org/mathematician-solves-computer-science-conjecture-in-two-pages-20190725/ Decades-Old Computer Science Conjecture Solved in Two Pages] by Erica Klarreich, [[Quanta Magazine]], July 25, 2019</ref>

Huang received an [[National Science Foundation CAREER Awards|NSF Career Award]] in 2019<ref>{{Cite web|title=NSF Award Search: Award#1945200 - CAREER: Algebraic Methods in Extremal Combinatorics|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=1945200&HistoricalAwards=false|access-date=2020-10-03|website=www.nsf.gov}}</ref> and a [[Sloan Research Fellowship]] in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2020 Fellows|url=https://sloan.org/fellowships/2020-Fellows|access-date=2020-10-03|website=sloan.org|archive-date=2020-09-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200925071515/https://sloan.org/fellowships/2020-Fellows|url-status=dead}}</ref>
